pubcol-w-3f0bf4972ef54264.definition_en: supporting or approving of someone or something
pubcol-w-3f0bf4972ef54264.example_simple: Most of the students were in favor of the new timetable.
pubcol-w-3f0bf4972ef54264.example_complex: The committee ruled in favor of the proposal after weeks of heated debate over its likely costs.

pubcol-w-d39bf57bf981b16d.definition_en: crying a great deal; weeping uncontrollably
collocations: leave someone in floods of tears
end up in floods of tears
pubcol-w-d39bf57bf981b16d.example_simple: She was in floods of tears when she heard the sad news.
pubcol-w-d39bf57bf981b16d.example_complex: By the end of the film the whole audience was in floods of tears, moved by the family's reunion.
pubcol-w-d39bf57bf981b16d.vi_meaning_correction: khóc nức nở, đầm đìa nước mắt

pubcol-w-b505c261c22e3c62.definition_en: usually; considering something as a whole rather than in detail
pubcol-w-b505c261c22e3c62.example_simple: In general, I prefer tea to coffee.
pubcol-w-b505c261c22e3c62.example_complex: In general, students who read widely tend to write more fluently, though there are always exceptions.

pubcol-w-c6a46fdb4fec47c2.definition_en: in order to show respect or admiration for someone or something
pubcol-w-c6a46fdb4fec47c2.example_simple: They held a party in honour of her retirement.
pubcol-w-c6a46fdb4fec47c2.example_complex: The university established a scholarship in honour of the professor who had devoted his life to marine research.

pubcol-w-284a01cb04812e33.definition_en: in a situation of danger or at risk of loss or failure
pubcol-w-284a01cb04812e33.example_simple: His job was in jeopardy after the company lost money.
pubcol-w-284a01cb04812e33.example_complex: A single careless comment to the press put the entire peace negotiation in jeopardy.

pubcol-w-199aa6e1d2817289.definition_en: according to what I think or believe
pubcol-w-199aa6e1d2817289.example_simple: In my view, the film was too long.
pubcol-w-199aa6e1d2817289.example_complex: In my view, the government should invest far more in public transport before widening the motorways.

pubcol-w-321d2aeba490cf9d.definition_en: used to introduce a clearer or simpler restatement of something
pubcol-w-321d2aeba490cf9d.example_simple: He said no — in other words, he refused to help.
pubcol-w-321d2aeba490cf9d.example_complex: The scheme was, in other words, a polite way of cutting staff without admitting to redundancies.

pubcol-w-84313b42d81dde4e.example_simple: I enjoy sports, football in particular.
pubcol-w-84313b42d81dde4e.example_complex: The report criticised several departments, and the finance team in particular, for poor record-keeping.

pubcol-w-7aafe489f55281ef.definition_en: by meeting someone rather than by phone, letter or online
pubcol-w-7aafe489f55281ef.example_simple: I'd like to thank her in person.
pubcol-w-7aafe489f55281ef.example_complex: Although we had exchanged emails for months, meeting the author in person gave the collaboration a new energy.

pubcol-w-7fa32470ed1cc33f.definition_en: rather than; chosen instead of something else
pubcol-w-7fa32470ed1cc33f.example_simple: She drinks water in preference to soft drinks.
pubcol-w-7fa32470ed1cc33f.example_complex: Many commuters now cycle in preference to driving, citing both cost and their own health.

pubcol-w-17bf13d05ea5ebeb.definition_en: in a place or situation where other people are present
pubcol-w-17bf13d05ea5ebeb.example_simple: He was too shy to sing in public.
pubcol-w-17bf13d05ea5ebeb.example_complex: The minister rarely admits doubts in public, however uncertain he may be behind closed doors.

pubcol-w-2b5e7119abb02c1d.definition_en: being talked about or considered; under discussion
pubcol-w-2b5e7119abb02c1d.example_simple: The book in question is out of print.
pubcol-w-2b5e7119abb02c1d.example_complex: On the evening in question, the witness claims to have seen the suspect leaving the building.

pubcol-w-248b675e2aa55a7e.definition_en: as a reaction to or reply to something
pubcol-w-248b675e2aa55a7e.example_simple: She smiled in response to his joke.
pubcol-w-248b675e2aa55a7e.example_complex: In response to falling sales, the company completely redesigned its product range within a year.

pubcol-w-a13beca777076567.definition_en: as payment or an exchange for something
pubcol-w-a13beca777076567.example_simple: He fixed my bike in return for a meal.
pubcol-w-a13beca777076567.example_complex: The volunteers asked for nothing in return for their work, save the chance to learn new skills.

pubcol-w-6dcbfaa6ad40f25a.definition_en: available and ready to eat because it is the natural time of year for it
pubcol-w-6dcbfaa6ad40f25a.example_simple: Strawberries are cheaper when they are in season.
pubcol-w-6dcbfaa6ad40f25a.example_complex: Cooking with produce that is in season not only tastes better but also cuts the cost of importing food out of season.

pubcol-w-e0236c785499ad78.definition_en: within a brief span of time; quickly
collocations: learn in a short period of time
grow in a short period of time
achieve in a short period of time
pubcol-w-e0236c785499ad78.example_simple: She learned to swim in a short period of time.
pubcol-w-e0236c785499ad78.example_complex: The start-up managed to double its customer base in a short period of time, largely through word of mouth.

pubcol-w-f7ee1edcc77bc464.definition_en: during a particular era or period defined by something
collocations: in the age of the internet
in the age of social media
pubcol-w-f7ee1edcc77bc464.example_simple: In the age of the internet, news travels very fast.
pubcol-w-f7ee1edcc77bc464.example_complex: In the age of artificial intelligence, workers are increasingly expected to retrain several times over their careers.

pubcol-w-623d7cea37756473.definition_en: during a hard or challenging period
collocations: stand by someone in difficult times
pubcol-w-623d7cea37756473.example_simple: Good friends help you in difficult times.
pubcol-w-623d7cea37756473.example_complex: In difficult times, communities that share resources tend to recover far more quickly than isolated households.

pubcol-w-15c329ad8d492fdf.definition_en: finally, after a lot of time, thought or effort
pubcol-w-15c329ad8d492fdf.example_simple: In the end, we decided to stay at home.
pubcol-w-15c329ad8d492fdf.example_complex: The negotiations dragged on for weeks, but in the end both sides accepted a modest compromise.

pubcol-w-69f477009576bc2b.definition_en: at the last possible moment, just before it is too late
collocations: arrive in the nick of time
saved in the nick of time
just in the nick of time
pubcol-w-69f477009576bc2b.example_simple: The doctor arrived in the nick of time to save him.
pubcol-w-69f477009576bc2b.example_complex: The firefighters reached the top floor in the nick of time, moments before the ceiling collapsed.

pubcol-w-e00b83084baecdb1.example_simple: I saw your photo in the paper this morning.
pubcol-w-e00b83084baecdb1.example_complex: The scandal was splashed across the front page, and for a week it was all anyone in the paper wrote about.
